title: Noncovalent interactions in large biomolecules
body: In large biomolecules or polymers, noncovalent interactions may occur between different molecules or between different regions of the same large biomolecule. The functionality and properties of such molecules depend strongly on the shape of the molecule, which is largely dictated by noncovalent interactions.
ced_evidence: 3.1.A.5 and 3.2.A.7: "noncovalent interactions may occur between different molecules or between different regions of the same large biomolecule"

title: Chromatography
body: Chromatography (paper, thin-layer, and column) separates chemical species by taking advantage of the differential strength of intermolecular interactions between and among the components of the solution (the mobile phase) and with the surface components of the stationary phase. The resulting chromatogram can be used to infer the relative polarities of components in a mixture.
ced_evidence: 3.9.A.1: "Chromatography (paper, thin-layer, and column) separates chemical species by taking advantage of the differential strength of intermolecular interactions"
